questions.question: What is Lambda Architecture?

options.text: A data processing architecture with batch layer, speed layer, and serving layer

questions.explanation: Lambda Architecture (Nathan Marz): handles massive data with both batch and real-time processing. Batch layer: complete, accurate. Speed layer: low-latency, approximate. Serving layer: merges both for queries.

questions.question: What is the batch layer in Lambda Architecture?

options.text: Processes all historical data to produce accurate batch views

questions.explanation: Batch layer: processes complete dataset. Immutable, append-only master data. Recomputes views from scratch. Accurate but high latency (hours). Technologies: Hadoop MapReduce, Spark batch.

questions.question: What is the speed layer in Lambda Architecture?

options.text: Processes recent data in real-time to compensate for batch layer latency

questions.explanation: Speed layer: real-time processing of recent data. Low latency, incremental updates. Views expire when batch catches up. Technologies: Storm, Spark Streaming, Flink. Trades accuracy for speed.

questions.question: What is the serving layer in Lambda Architecture?

options.text: Indexes and exposes batch and speed layer outputs for low-latency queries

questions.explanation: Serving layer: merges batch views + real-time views. Responds to queries. Technologies: Druid, Cassandra, HBase. Query = batch_result + speed_result. Provides complete, up-to-date answers.

questions.question: What is the main criticism of Lambda Architecture?

options.text: Complexity of maintaining two separate codebases for batch and speed layers

questions.explanation: Lambda criticism: dual codebase (batch logic + streaming logic). Same computation, different implementations. Maintenance burden, potential inconsistencies. Led to Kappa Architecture alternative.

questions.question: How does Lambda Architecture handle late-arriving data?

options.text: Batch layer reprocesses all data, eventually incorporating late arrivals

questions.explanation: Late data handling: batch layer recomputes from master dataset. Late data in master → next batch run includes it. Speed layer may miss it, but batch corrects. Eventually consistent.

questions.question: What is the master dataset in Lambda Architecture?

options.text: An immutable, append-only store of all raw data—the source of truth

questions.explanation: Master dataset: immutable, append-only. Contains all raw events ever received. Source of truth. Batch layer reads from it. Can always recompute any view. Stored in HDFS, S3, etc.

questions.question: What technologies are commonly used for the batch layer?

options.text: Hadoop MapReduce, Apache Spark batch, Hive

questions.explanation: Batch layer technologies: Hadoop MapReduce (original), Spark batch (faster), Hive (SQL interface). Process large datasets, produce batch views. Run periodically (hourly, daily).

questions.question: What technologies are commonly used for the speed layer?

options.text: Apache Storm, Spark Streaming, Apache Flink, Kafka Streams

questions.explanation: Speed layer technologies: Storm (original), Spark Streaming, Flink (modern), Kafka Streams. Process events as they arrive. Sub-second latency. Incremental view updates.

questions.question: How do batch and speed layer views get merged?

options.text: Query time merge—serving layer combines batch view with speed layer increments

questions.explanation: View merging: at query time. Batch view (complete but stale) + speed view (recent increments). Example: total_count = batch_count + realtime_count. Serving layer handles merge logic.

questions.question: When is Lambda Architecture a good choice?

options.text: When you need both historical accuracy and real-time insights on massive datasets

questions.explanation: Lambda fits: massive scale, need both accurate historical analysis and real-time dashboards. Examples: social media analytics, IoT monitoring, fraud detection. Trade-off: complexity for completeness.

questions.question: Your analytics platform needs accurate daily reports AND real-time dashboards. What architecture?

options.text: Lambda Architecture—batch layer for accurate reports, speed layer for real-time dashboards

questions.explanation: Dual requirement = Lambda. Batch: nightly job computes accurate aggregates for reports. Speed: streaming updates real-time dashboard. Serving: queries merge both. Complete and timely.
